root_cause: Fa0/2 is on default VLAN 1 instead of VLAN 10, so PC2 is in a different broadcast domain than PC1.
evidence: show vlan brief lists Fa0/2 under VLAN1; interface config shows switchport access vlan 1.
fix_steps: interface fa0/2; switchport access vlan 10

root_cause: VLAN 20 is not in the trunk's allowed VLAN list on SW1.
evidence: show interfaces trunk on SW1 lists allowed vlans 10,30 only, missing 20.
fix_steps: switchport trunk allowed vlan add 20 on SW1

root_cause: Fa0/5 was never assigned to VLAN 30 and remains on default VLAN 1.
evidence: show interfaces fa0/5 switchport shows Access Mode VLAN: 1 (default).
fix_steps: switchport access vlan 30 on fa0/5

root_cause: Sub-interface Gi0/0.30 is administratively down.
evidence: show ip interface brief shows Gi0/0.30 administratively down.
fix_steps: no shutdown on gi0/0.30 (verify encapsulation dot1Q 30 and IP too)

root_cause: The IP phone is not receiving power/registering correctly, likely a PoE issue.
evidence: Phone registers but PC behind it has no access; insufficient evidence to isolate further.
fix_steps: Check PoE budget on the switch

root_cause: SW2's VTP configuration revision is stale and needs to be reset.
evidence: VTP status shows matching revision numbers but VLAN 40 missing on SW2.
fix_steps: Reset SW2's VTP revision counter and re-sync

root_cause: PC1's default gateway (192.168.1.100) does not match R1's interface IP (192.168.1.1).
evidence: ipconfig shows gateway 192.168.1.100; show ip interface brief shows Gi0/0 is 192.168.1.1.
fix_steps: Set PC1 gateway to 192.168.1.1

root_cause: The VLAN 10 SVI is administratively down, so it cannot route as the gateway.
evidence: show ip interface brief shows Vlan10 administratively down.
fix_steps: no shutdown on interface vlan10

root_cause: ip routing is not enabled globally on the multilayer switch.
evidence: show ip route has no connected SVI entries; 'ip routing' absent from running-config.
fix_steps: Enable 'ip routing' globally

root_cause: The DHCP relay agent is not configured on the VLAN 30 interface.
evidence: Clients on VLAN 30 get an address but no gateway; the pool section shown is incomplete.
fix_steps: Add ip helper-address on the VLAN 30 SVI

root_cause: Subnet mask mismatch between the server (/25) and the router interface (/24) on the same segment.
evidence: Server subnet mask is 255.255.255.128 (/25) while router interface is /24.
fix_steps: Correct server mask to 255.255.255.0

root_cause: Missing ip helper-address on the VLAN 40 SVI, so DHCP broadcasts never reach the DHCP server.
evidence: show ip dhcp binding has no VLAN40 entries; no ip helper-address on interface vlan40.
fix_steps: ip helper-address 10.0.0.1 on interface vlan40

root_cause: The DHCP pool for VLAN 10 is too small (/28) for the number of hosts, exhausting available addresses.
evidence: show ip dhcp pool shows Total addresses 14, Leased 14, Available 0.
fix_steps: Widen the pool to a /24

root_cause: A duplicate/legacy DHCP pool (TESTPOOL) is overlapping and serving the wrong gateway.
evidence: Two pools cover 192.168.20.0/24; TESTPOOL hands out gateway 192.168.99.1.
fix_steps: Remove the duplicate TESTPOOL

root_cause: Static printer IP was never excluded from the DHCP pool, causing a duplicate/conflicting lease.
evidence: show ip dhcp conflict lists 192.168.10.50 with a ping conflict.
fix_steps: ip dhcp excluded-address 192.168.10.50 192.168.10.50

root_cause: A specific host on VLAN 50 has a firewall blocking DHCP broadcasts.
evidence: No DHCP conflict or binding logged for VLAN 50; limited evidence given.
fix_steps: Check host firewall settings

root_cause: The DNS A record for fileserver.corp.local does not exist on the DNS server.
evidence: nslookup returns NXDOMAIN for fileserver.corp.local even though the DNS server itself answers.
fix_steps: Add/correct the A record on the DNS server

root_cause: The DHCP pool for VLAN 10 never specifies a dns-server, so clients have no resolver configured.
evidence: show ip dhcp pool VLAN10POOL has no dns-server line.
fix_steps: Add dns-server line to the pool

root_cause: The affected PC's network cable or NIC driver is faulty.
evidence: Only one PC on the VLAN is affected; insufficient evidence to isolate DNS vs link-layer cause.
fix_steps: Swap the cable / reinstall the NIC driver

root_cause: The internal DNS server has no forwarder configured for external domain queries.
evidence: Internal names resolve; external names like www.example.com do not; no forwarder in DNS server config.
fix_steps: Configure a forwarder (e.g., 8.8.8.8)

root_cause: R1's static route destination network has a typo (192.168.3.0 instead of 192.168.2.0).
evidence: show ip route has no entry for 192.168.2.0/24; configured static route targets 192.168.3.0/24.
fix_steps: Correct the static route to 192.168.2.0 255.255.255.0

root_cause: R1 and R2 are configured with mismatched OSPF process IDs, preventing adjacency.
evidence: show ip ospf neighbor is empty on both routers; process numbers differ in the configs shown.
fix_steps: Match the OSPF process IDs on both routers

root_cause: The static route for 192.168.99.0/24 points to a next-hop IP that is not a real device on that subnet.
evidence: show ip route shows the static route via 192.168.1.254, which does not exist on that network.
fix_steps: Correct the next-hop to the real router interface IP

root_cause: R3, the new transit router, has no routing protocol or static routes configured.
evidence: show ip route on R3 only shows connected routes, nothing toward R2's LAN.
fix_steps: Configure OSPF or static routes on R3

root_cause: A duplex mismatch on one of the equal-cost links is causing CRC errors and intermittent loss.
evidence: Gi0/1 on R1 is half-duplex while the far end on R2 is full-duplex, with high CRC/input errors.
fix_steps: Set both ends to the same duplex/speed

root_cause: OSPF adjacency between R1 and R2 has failed due to a hello/dead timer mismatch.
evidence: Neighbors show FULL is mentioned, but the summarized route is missing from R1's table.
fix_steps: Match hello/dead timers on both routers

root_cause: ACL 101 only permits ICMP to the server and implicitly denies all other traffic, including the TCP ports needed for file/web access.
evidence: show access-lists 101 has a permit icmp line then an explicit deny ip any any with no TCP permits.
fix_steps: Add permit tcp lines for the needed ports (e.g., 445, 80) above the deny

root_cause: The GUEST-ACL exists with correct rules but was never applied to the VLAN 60 interface.
evidence: show running-config interface vlan60 has no ip access-group applied.
fix_steps: Apply: ip access-group GUEST-ACL in on interface vlan60

root_cause: The ADMIN-ACL access-class is missing from the VTY lines entirely.
evidence: ACL exists and is referenced under line vty, but the direction of the permit statement looked reversed.
fix_steps: Re-apply access-class ADMIN-ACL in on the VTY lines

root_cause: ACL 110 has only a deny statement, so the implicit deny-all at the end blocks all traffic, not just the intended subnet.
evidence: show access-lists 110 shows one deny line and no permit statements.
fix_steps: Add 'permit ip any any' as the final line

root_cause: The inside LAN interface (Gi0/0) is missing 'ip nat inside', so NAT never triggers.
evidence: show ip nat translations is empty; ip nat inside source list 1 ... overload exists but Gi0/0 config lacks 'ip nat inside'.
fix_steps: Add 'ip nat inside' on interface gi0/0

root_cause: The ISP link itself is down, so no NAT translations can succeed.
evidence: Static NAT is unreachable from outside; insufficient evidence given about the WAN link status.
fix_steps: Check the WAN interface status

root_cause: The NAT overload ACL (ACL 1) does not include the 192.168.50.0/24 network, so it is never translated.
evidence: show access-lists 1 only permits 192.168.10.0/24 and 192.168.20.0/24.
fix_steps: access-list 1 permit 192.168.50.0 0.0.0.255

root_cause: Missing ip helper-address on the VLAN 15 SVI, so wireless DHCP requests never reach the DHCP server.
evidence: show running-config interface vlan15 has no ip helper-address configured.
fix_steps: Add ip helper-address 10.0.0.1 on interface vlan15

root_cause: Both APs are on the same channel with overlapping coverage, causing co-channel interference.
evidence: AP1 and AP2 are both on channel 6 with max power and overlapping coverage.
fix_steps: Move AP2 to a non-overlapping channel (1 or 11)

root_cause: GUEST-ACL was never applied to the VLAN 60 interface.
evidence: Guest Wi-Fi devices can reach the internal server directly.
fix_steps: Apply ip access-group GUEST-ACL in on interface vlan60
